page.layout: One page of running text under a woodcut ornament at the top. The title block (DISPUTATIO TEXTUALIS, subtitle, De REGENERATIONE, Greek epigraph) is at full width, followed by THESIS I, a paragraph, "II.", and a paragraph ending in a line-end catchword. The faint text in both margins is show-through from the reverse side and is not transcribed. Signature "A 2" at the foot, left of centre. No page number and no running head.

main_text.head: DISPUTATIO TEXTUALIS. Theologica ex Joh. 3. v. 5. De REGENERATIONE.
main_text.p: Ἐὰν μὴ τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
main_text.head: THESIS I.
main_text.p: ΕΝΟΣ δὲ χρεία[?]: sic respondit olim Christus Jesus Servator noster Marthæ, Luc. 10. v. 41. quæ suprà modum sollicita erat, & de multis satagebat, tacitè eam arguens τῆς πολυπραγμοσύνης[?], dùm ipsi non multa, sed unum ostendit, de quo debeat esse sollicita, nempè regnum cœlorum, unum necessarium, quo qui fruitur, omnia possidet, qui verò caret, omnibus caret: & quemadmodum regnum cælorum unum illud est, ad quod assequendum tendere debemus, ita unum est medium eò nos ducens, nempè Christus Jesus cum suis beneficiis, ex quorum primis est Regeneratio, de cujus necessitate ad regnum Dei consequendum Christus ipse Nicodemo concionatur, tùm in toto contextu, tùm in hoc ipso textu; cujus considerabimus occasionem, scopum & argumentum.

page.notes: Thesis heading "THESIS I." is set as a level 2 heading because it stands alone in spaced capitals. The Greek epigraph and the Greek phrases in the first paragraph are doubtful in places (marked [?]), notably the accent and iota-subscript forms and the word πολυπραγμοσύνης. The drop-cap E of the first paragraph is joined to ΕΝΟΣ. The marginal text on both sides is show-through and was left out.
